page: Microsoft Azure E16-4as_v7 is a constrained-vCPU memory-optimized virtual machine operating on Microsoft Hyper-V. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at up to 4.5 GHz, the instance allocates 4 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware instruction sets such as AVX-512 (f, vnni, bf16) and cryptographic accelerators.

The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding an extensive memory-to-vCPU density of 32.0 GB per core. It includes no bundled local ephemeral storage and features zero GPUs. Performance benchmarks show top-tier single-threaded capability, scoring 3631.57 in stress-ng single-core tests, 40.09 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression, and 17.35 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Large-block uncached memory bandwidth reaches 46.95 GB/sec for reads and 33.73 GB/sec for writes.

Due to its restricted 4 vCPU allocation, multi-threaded throughput is constrained, registering average performance across multi-core stress-ng (7229.58) and weak results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. The machine maintains steady in-memory performance, achieving 7.77 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads. Qualitative cost efficiency stems from its constrained CPU model, allowing memory-heavy architectures to minimize software licensing fees that scale per core.

Microsoft Azure E16-4as_v7 is tailored for workloads requiring significant memory capacity without high parallel CPU core counts, such as caching nodes, in-memory key-value databases, and licensed relational databases that operate efficiently within a 4-vCPU footprint.
description: Microsoft Azure E16-4as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz and 128.0 GB of RAM. Configured with a 32.0 GB per vCPU ratio, it incorporates 32 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 vector instructions. The instance offers no local disk storage and contains no discrete GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate top-tier single-core compute and decompression execution, balanced by average multi-core processing in line with its 4-vCPU capacity. In memory benchmarks, it delivers 46.95 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and achieves 7.77 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads. This profile provides architectural and licensing cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that require substantial RAM allocations with moderate compute footprints, including in-memory key-value stores, enterprise caches, and memory-bound databases.
